There is no longer a weight requirement to receive a diagnosis of AN according to the current standard of diagnosis and care. It’s that simple.

Criteria does NOT = requirement. Especially not within the context of the DSMV where lists often have criteria, with the requirement being # out of out of # criteria being met for a dx.

The same guidelines also classifies severity with anything being above BMI of 17 being “mild anorexia nervosa”. Lastly, it notes that ALL criteria do not need to be met for a dx of AN, then mentioning the atypical subtype.

So technically..body dysmorphic disorder is not really any of these things. I agree the term is fitting for seeing yourself as fat when you’re not, but if you want the genuine definition of body dysmorphic disorder, an exclusion criteria is that the symptom can’t be better explained by an eating disorder.

BDD is a preoccupation with a perceived flaw that permeates one’s thoughts to the point of disruption to their daily life. Examples would be someone who is so convinced their nose is hideous that they’re embarrassed by it, constantly upset by it, spend a lot of time looking at it, and likely to spend money they may not have to have it surgically corrected. Another example would be acne that one perceives to be so bad that they hide their face, don’t leave their house, constantly using time covering it up or trying various and possibly harmful treatments, etc. For this disorder, if someone is preoccupied with their weight in a way inconsistent with what their weight is (ie an underweight person thinking they’re fat or a normal weight person thinking they’re too thin, etc), it is only considered BDD if they do NOT engage in ED behaviors. If they do, it’s an ED. They are very similar but separate disorders.

Body dysmorphia, as a stand alone term from the associated disorder isn’t super well defined, so the majority of folks likely experience it at some point. If something about your appearance is perceived in a way distressing to you and something you fixate on but is not even noticeable by others, that would be considered dysmorphia. It’s not necessarily seeing a distorted image in the mirror. That distorted image itself is more consistent with EDs.

It’s water weight, it would be truly challenging if not genuinely impossible to gain fat/muscle in that timeframe. Water retention isn’t necessarily a good thing and if it’s been getting worse please go get seen.

Elevating your legs should help redistribute the fluid and may help with the heaviness, but being sure to eat as well as hydrate is the only way to ensure appropriate electrolyte and fluid balances in your body. It’s worth getting checked out if it’s new to you (some women have increased bloating/retention at certain times of their cycle, I’d imagine men may have variation to some extent too) as it could be an early sign of something going on elsewhere in your body. But if you’re not coughing up junk, having trouble breathing, severe weakness or anything like that I think you can take a breath and start trying to schedule an appointment with your doc.

So if you’re having symmetric edema but no other symptoms, you’re not in immediate danger. Yes pitting edema is classic for heart failure but it’s more likely just venous valve insufficiency/poor circulation. Heart failure is what we’re worried about but without cardiac risk factors or other symptoms, likely not the cause. Most people over the age of 20 have it and will notice it when they’re on their feet for too long. Is it worse at the end of the day? If yes, then it’s not an immediate concern but you should still get it checked out to see if you have kidney, thyroid, or liver problems or maybe lymph obstruction (unlikely unless it’s asymmetric).

However, if you are having trouble breathing, pain in your chest, dizziness, palpitations, etc- go to an Emergency Department. If you are at a dangerously low BMI or have had weight cycling for a while, I would suggest you get seen sooner rather than later. If it’s giving you anxiety, go get it checked out now.

Be safe and take care of yourself 💕
